correctness.rationale: Exact generator, resolvent and resultant reconstructed algebraically; roots simple by Jacobi symmetrization. Simple resultant cancellation at c=1 proves middle spectral sign reversal; positive spectral coefficients for c>=1 force decreasing hazard. For c<1 a two-exponential sign-variation argument proves one and only one stationary point, with initial derivative -1/4-c and eventual derivative positive. Two-state subgenerator proves 1-2 habitat impossibility. Extracted standalone verification passed 56 labeled-vs-lumped Markov computations and exact symbolic checks.

value.rationale: The sharp c/e=1 boundary identifies when the age of an extant regional population first reduces and then increases its instantaneous extinction risk, versus consistently reduces that risk. This full-threshold statement in a recolonizing model is not a simple declaration that mixture hazards can be nonmonotone. The exact minimum of three habitats distinguishes genuine latent patch aggregation effects from two-patch models; useful as an analytically checkable benchmark for regional extinction surveillance. It makes no field efficacy claim.
